title: Check yourself: Continue, resume and fork: what a session keeps

questions.stem: A review agent finished mapping a payments module on Monday. On Tuesday the team wants to compare a rewrite with a refactor from that same baseline, and the Monday thread must stay usable. What should the SDK call carry?

options.text: `resume` with the saved id and `fork_session` enabled
options.says: Fork is an option set together with a resume id, so it branches a copy and leaves the original usable.

options.text: `continue_conversation` alone, which branches the latest run
options.says: Ruled out because "**Continue** finds the most recent session in the current directory", so it adds to that session and branches nothing.

options.text: `resume` with the saved id, once for each approach
options.says: Ruled out because "Continue and resume both pick up an existing session and add to it", which puts both approaches into one history.

options.text: A new run whose first prompt only names the Monday thread
options.says: Ruled out because a name carries none of the analysis, and the guide says to "Capture the results you need (analysis output, decisions, file diffs) as application state and pass them into a fresh session's prompt."

questions.stem: A multi-user app keeps one conversation per customer. After a restart it must return each customer to the right earlier conversation, not just the latest one. What does the code store for each customer?

options.text: A `continue` flag, with one working directory for each customer
options.says: Ruled out because "**Continue** finds the most recent session in the current directory", so a customer would get the latest conversation only and never an earlier one.

options.text: A display name for each customer, passed to `resume` in the SDK
options.says: Ruled out because "Resume takes a specific session ID", not a display name; the guide's `--resume <session-name>` is a command-line form, and the SDK guide passes an id.

options.text: The session id from the last result message
options.says: Resume needs a specific id, and the result carries it on every result.

options.text: A fork of the first session, created for each customer
options.says: Ruled out because "Fork is different: it creates a new session that starts with a copy of the original's history", which is a second conversation and not a return to the first.
